entry_rule.rule_text: volatility (ATR) expanding (mult=1.11) AND MACD line above signal

interpretation: A standalone trend-state filter (MACD line above signal): it stays 'on' for as long as the condition holds, so it behaves more like a persistent regime gate than a precisely timed trigger -- expect it to fire often, in clusters, and for the per-trade edge to come from riding the broader trend rather than from precise entry timing. Risk model: stop at 1.13x ATR from entry, target at 4.20R (i.e. 4.75x ATR), max hold 15 bars, entries filled at the next bar's open to avoid lookahead. Realized: 22 trades, 64% win rate (Wilson 95% lower bound 43%), reward:risk 3.27, expectancy +1.43R/trade, profit factor 5.72. In this sample both win rate and reward:risk pull their weight here -- a robust, 'high win-rate AND high R:R' combination rather than leaning on one factor. Out-of-sample check: 14 trades, 50% win rate, expectancy +0.75R -- holds up out of sample.

entry_rule.rule_text: RSI oversold (period=14, threshold=35.0) AND stochastic oversold (period=14, threshold=14.3)

interpretation: A standalone mean-reversion entry (RSI oversold (period=14, threshold=35.0); stochastic oversold (period=14, threshold=14.3)) with no trend filter -- this is the riskiest archetype here, since it will also fire against strong downtrends. Its edge, if real, likely comes from a high win rate on quick reversion trades rather than trend participation. Risk model: stop at 1.89x ATR from entry, target at 2.90R (i.e. 5.48x ATR), max hold 59 bars, entries filled at the next bar's open to avoid lookahead. Realized: 33 trades, 64% win rate (Wilson 95% lower bound 47%), reward:risk 2.67, expectancy +1.16R/trade, profit factor 4.67. In this sample both win rate and reward:risk pull their weight here -- a robust, 'high win-rate AND high R:R' combination rather than leaning on one factor. Out-of-sample check: 18 trades, 61% win rate, expectancy +1.15R -- holds up out of sample.
